title: Cocktail 2 Cost ₹150 Crore to Make. Bollywood Has Never Spent This Much on a Love Story.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna headline Maddock Films' bet that the romantic comedy deserves blockbuster scale. The film releases June 19.
body:
Here is a number that should make you pause: ₹150 crore.

That is the total landing cost of Cocktail 2, according to a Bollywood Hungama exclusive — making it comfortably the most expensive romantic comedy in the history of Hindi cinema. The production budget alone is ₹95 crore. Actor fees account for another ₹35 crore, split between Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna. The remaining ₹20 crore goes to print and publicity. When a rom-com starts trading in the same budget territory as action blockbusters, something in the industry has shifted.

## The Bet

Dinesh Vijan and his Maddock Films banner have been on an extraordinary run. After the Stree and Munjya horror-comedy universe redefined what mid-budget Hindi films could earn, Vijan is now turning his attention to the genre that Bollywood was built on — and refusing to treat it as a small film.

Cocktail 2, directed by Homi Adajania who also helmed the 2012 original, is described as a spiritual successor rather than a direct sequel. The original Cocktail — starring Saif Ali Khan, Deepika Padukone, and Diana Penty — became a sleeper hit largely on the strength of its music and its willingness to let its female characters be complicated. The sequel carries the brand but presents an entirely new story and cast.

Shahid plays Kunal. Kriti Sanon takes on the role of Ally. Rashmika Mandanna plays Diya. The screenplay has been crafted by Tarun Jain and Luv Ranjan, and the film was reportedly shot over 70 days across multiple countries, with significant portions filmed in Sicily, Italy.

## The Music Factor

If the original Cocktail is remembered for anything beyond Deepika Padukone's Veronica, it is the music. The sequel's soundtrack, composed by Pritam Chakraborty, is already generating significant buzz. At a media preview event, two tracks were showcased: Mashooka, an energetic romantic number featuring Shahid and Kriti shot across Sicilian landscapes, and Tujhko, an emotional ballad sung by Arijit Singh centered on Shahid and Rashmika's characters. Attendees described the latter as a standout.

For a genre that has struggled commercially in the post-pandemic era, betting on music-driven, star-powered romance is either visionary or reckless. Maddock appears to be betting on visionary.

## The Numbers Game

Perhaps the most striking detail in the budget breakdown is that approximately 50 percent of the ₹150 crore investment has already been recovered through pre-sales — non-theatrical deals covering satellite, digital, and music rights. Maddock's brand equity in the market is clearly paying dividends. The film needs roughly ₹75 crore more from theatrical revenue to break even, a target that is ambitious but not unreasonable for a June tentpole with this cast and music.

## The NRI Angle

For the Indian diaspora, Cocktail 2 represents something the Hindi film industry has largely abandoned in recent years: the unapologetic, big-screen romantic entertainer. While Hollywood has all but killed the theatrical rom-com, Bollywood is doubling down with a budget that signals genuine belief in the genre. The original Cocktail was a film many NRIs discovered on streaming. This sequel wants them in the theater.

Whether audiences reward that conviction will say a great deal about where Hindi cinema goes next.

Cocktail 2 releases in theaters worldwide on June 19, 2026.
